description:
You are a researcher starting a deep learning literature review project. Your Zotero library has been pre-loaded with 18 research papers.

Your task: Create a hierarchical collection structure to organize your papers:

1. Create a top-level collection called exactly: 'Deep Learning Survey'
2. Inside 'Deep Learning Survey', create a subcollection called exactly: 'NLP Papers'
3. Inside 'Deep Learning Survey', create a subcollection called exactly: 'Vision Papers'
4. Move these papers into 'NLP Papers':
   - 'Attention Is All You Need' (Vaswani et al., 2017)
   - 'BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding' (Devlin et al., 2019)
   - 'Language Models are Few-Shot Learners' (Brown et al., 2020 - the GPT-3 paper)
5. Move these papers into 'Vision Papers':
   - 'ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks' (Krizhevsky et al., 2012 - AlexNet)
   - 'Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition' (He et al., 2016 - ResNet)
   - 'Generative Adversarial Nets' (Goodfellow et al., 2014 - GANs)

How to create collections in Zotero:
- Right-click on 'My Library' in the left panel and select 'New Collection'
- To create a subcollection, right-click on the parent collection and select 'New Subcollection'
- To add papers to a collection, drag them from the main list onto the collection name in the left panel
- You can also right-click a paper and use 'Add to Collection'

Note: The collection names must match exactly (case-sensitive).

nlp_papers: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
vision_papers: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
